terms.comment: The curved horn of the Roman army and the rites, made of bronze but named from the animal’s horn, as Varro explains (LL 5.117).
A crooked horn, the shepherd’s and the swineherd’s, and the army’s signal for the watches.

phrases.latin: būcinā īnflāvit, ut tanta circumflūxerit nōs cervōrum aprōrum et cēterārum quadripedum multitūdō
phrases.english: he blew a horn, and such a crowd of deer, boar and other beasts came streaming round us

sources: Lewis & Short: cornu · Lewis & Short: bucina
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. brass: French horn.
Varro from the Latinitas loci collection (loci-varro).
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 329.
